topics.label: Introduction to the Complement Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the topic of complement and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement Overview, Nomenclature, and C3 Mechanics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide the foundational overview, nomenclature rules, and central C3 activation mechanics essential to understanding complement.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three recognition pathways that drive complement initiation and threshold activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms triggered by complement to destroy or mark pathogens for clearance.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the regulatory factors and mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the clinical manifestations and disease presentations resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the evolutionary strategies pathogens utilize to evade complement-mediated killing, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing remarks concluding the complement lecture and previewing the next lecture topic.
